summary_of_change:
Despite short-term volume noise and tough winter catastrophe comparisons, Copart's core operational reality demonstrates robust underlying earning power and unyielding market leadership. In Q3 FY26 (ended April 30, 2026), consolidated revenue reached $1,237.1M (+2.1% YoY), translating to an annualized run-rate of $4,948.3M. While global unit volume contracted 2.4% YoY due to consumer auto policy retrenchment and higher deductibles, global Average Selling Prices (ASPs) expanded +4.6% YoY (with U.S. insurance ASPs up +4.1% to record levels), proving that Copart's global buyer network continues to yield unmatched recovery returns for consignors.

Operational margins remain industry-leading, supported by Copart's proprietary real estate footprint. Q3 FY26 Gross Margin expanded 71 basis points YoY to 46.3% ($572.6M), while U.S. gross margin reached 48.3%. Operating margin stood at a formidable 37.5% ($464.3M operating income). This profitability is anchored by structural total loss frequency trends, which hit an all-time record of 23.6% in early 2026. Non-insurance channels are expanding rapidly, highlighted by Purple Wave heavy equipment GTV compounding at over 25% LTM and international volumes rising +5.9% YoY (revenue +14.1% YoY).

Capital allocation has shifted aggressively toward return of capital and balance sheet optimization. Year-to-date through Q3 FY26, Copart deployed $1.63 billion to repurchase 43.4 million common shares, reducing diluted share count by 3.6% YoY to 942.8 million. With $4.2 billion in liquid cash and zero debt, returning CEO Jay Adair has signaled renewed focus on deploying excess cash toward global growth pillars, commercial whole car channels, and technology services while slowing land acquisition CapEx, ensuring that Copart's physical storage moat remains virtually unassailable.

summary_of_change:
Copart’s real-time operational engine demonstrates underlying resilience despite localized domestic insurance volume drag. Operating across 250+ physical locations in 11 countries, the platform continues to process over 4.0 million annual global vehicle auction transactions connecting 1.0 million registered buyers across 250+ physical locations in 11 countries. The latest quarter generated $1,237.4M in revenue ($4,949.6M annualized run-rate) with gross margins holding firm at 46.3% and operating margins remaining strong at 37.4%.

While U.S. insurance volumes experienced a 4.2% YoY decline due to cyclical consumer policy retrenchment, international unit volumes expanded 5.9% YoY, non-insurance commercial consignment via BluCar rose over 4%, and heavy equipment platform Purple Wave surged over 25% in trailing gross transaction value. Crucially, total loss frequency reached an all-time record of 23.6%, demonstrating that increasing vehicle technological complexity continues to push insurers toward declaring vehicles total losses.

what_was_before:
Despite short-term volume noise and tough winter catastrophe comparisons, Copart's core operational reality demonstrates robust underlying earning power and unyielding market leadership. In Q3 FY26 (ended April 30, 2026), consolidated revenue reached $1,237.1M (+2.1% YoY), translating to an annualized run-rate of $4,948.3M. While global unit volume contracted 2.4% YoY due to consumer auto policy retrenchment and higher deductibles, global Average Selling Prices (ASPs) expanded +4.6% YoY (with U.S. insurance ASPs up +4.1% to record levels), proving that Copart's global buyer network continues to yield unmatched recovery returns for consignors.

Operational margins remain industry-leading, supported by Copart's proprietary real estate footprint. Q3 FY26 Gross Margin expanded 71 basis points YoY to 46.3% ($572.6M), while U.S. gross margin reached 48.3%. Operating margin stood at a formidable 37.5% ($464.3M operating income). This profitability is anchored by structural total loss frequency trends, which hit an all-time record of 23.6% in early 2026. Non-insurance channels are expanding rapidly, highlighted by Purple Wave heavy equipment GTV compounding at over 25% LTM and international volumes rising +5.9% YoY (revenue +14.1% YoY).

Capital allocation has shifted aggressively toward return of capital and balance sheet optimization. Year-to-date through Q3 FY26, Copart deployed $1.63 billion to repurchase 43.4 million common shares, reducing diluted share count by 3.6% YoY to 942.8 million. With $4.2 billion in liquid cash and zero debt, returning CEO Jay Adair has signaled renewed focus on deploying excess cash toward global growth pillars, commercial whole car channels, and technology services while slowing land acquisition CapEx, ensuring that Copart's physical storage moat remains virtually unassailable.

market_pricing_in:
Skepticism surrounding Copart ($33.26) stems from a visible operational disconnect between contracting core U.S. insurance volumes and top-line growth sustained largely by elevated vehicle selling prices. Mr. Market is concerned that consolidated U.S. insurance auction volumes dropped 4.2% YoY in recent quarterly filings as auto insurance premium inflation forced cash-strapped motorists to drop collision coverage or raise deductibles. Skeptics argue that temporary Average Selling Price (ASP) tailwinds are masking underlying unit processing decay, leaving Copart exposed to significant margin compression once used car prices normalize.

Furthermore, investors fear competitive market share erosion and long-term technological disruption. Following RB Global’s acquisition and integration of Insurance Auto Auctions (IAA), major insurance carriers are actively allocating volumes away from Copart to avoid vendor lock-in, resulting in a positive volume differential for RB Global. Concurrently, the long-term adoption of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) raises terminal concerns regarding accident frequency reductions. Consequently, the market prices Copart at 22.0x P/OE, treating current owner cash flows as cyclically peak earnings subject to structural headwinds.
